name: Squeeze-failure fade — bb_z overshoot re-entry (1h)
rationale: ECONOMIC MECHANISM (the squeeze-failure fade at 1h reading the failed poke via the band z-score bb_z rather than range_position — a standardized-distance gauge that keys off statistical over-extension, so it is a distinct crowding read from the raw-range versions): a bb_width multi-window floor is a coiled spring; a downside break that fails and snaps back is a false breakdown that trapped the breakdown crowd, whose buy-to-cover fuels the reversion. 2025 BB backtests show naive band-breaks are a coin-flip because false breaks dominate — the failed break is the edge, not the break. Entry (long): bb_width below a fitted floor (spring) AND bb_z below a fitted floor (price statistically stretched below the band -> the overshoot poke) AND rsi in washout (momentum exhausted on the poke). Hold for the snap-back. The counterparty is the mechanical band-break sellers; their stops are our fuel. Distinct from squeeze-then-trend (buys the confirmed break) and from the 15m/30m variants (raw-range vs standardized-z over-extension). Exit: bb_z crosses up through a fitted level (mean-reverted back toward the band) or stop/TP/time. DISCONFIRMER 1: drop the bb_width squeeze pre-condition — if fading any bb_z overshoot works as well, the squeeze is inert and this is a generic z-score dip-buy (already in the inbox), not a squeeze-family edge. DISCONFIRMER 2: if bb_z-floor and rsi-floor fire on the same bars >80% of the time they are one over-extension gauge -> drop one. DISCONFIRMER 3: net of ~20bps at 1h the fades must clear per-trade.
catalyst: a squeeze whose downside break statistically overshoots and fails
